finding.claim: Scheduler webhook accepts unauthenticated requests when no token is configured: the token check is skipped when webhookToken is empty, so any remote caller can force-run a job by ID or run all due jobs.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP request to the scheduler webhook endpoint with optional ?job= query parameter (SchedulerController.php:86-95)
finding.sink: Scheduler::processWebhookTrigger() runs a job in the foreground (Scheduler.php:1102-1104) or all due jobs (Scheduler.php:1121) and returns job output (Scheduler.php:1114)

trace.note: Reads Authorization Bearer header; token is null when absent
if ($this->webhookToken && $token !== $this->webhookToken) — when configured token is empty the check is skipped entirely
getJob($jobId) then run in foreground, ignoring schedule
Job output returned in HTTP response
webhookEnabled loaded from modernConfig; webhookToken loaded at 579 with null default (Scheduler.php:70)
Ships enabled:false and token:null; comment says 'Set a secure token' but nothing enforces it

finding.guards_checked: Enable toggle scheduler.modern.webhook.enabled (SchedulerController.php:81, Scheduler.php:578) is the only gate that applies. isWebhookEnabled() (Scheduler.php:625-634) also requires plugins.scheduler-webhook.enabled, but processWebhookTrigger() does not call it. Token comparison is non-constant-time (!==, Scheduler.php:1091), a minor secondary issue. Precondition: admin enables webhook and leaves token unset. Route registration lives in the external scheduler-webhook plugin, not in this tree, so reachability is unconfirmed (medium confidence).
